safety_signals: Systolic blood pressure increased by 5.4 mm Hg vs baseline in the torcetrapib arm (off-target pressor effect)
Decreased serum potassium with increased serum sodium, bicarbonate, and aldosterone (off-target mineralocorticoid effect)
Increased risk of major cardiovascular events (HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.09-1.44)

Trial terminated early for increased death and cardiac events; described as an off-target effect of torcetrapib of unknown mechanism, though adverse effects related to CETP inhibition could not be excluded
note: Agent-curated from PubMed via the Claude PubMed MCP. According to PubMed, Barter PJ et al., 'Effects of torcetrapib in patients at high risk for coronary events,' N Engl J Med 2007;357(21):2109-2122 (DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa0706628, PMID 17984165). NCT00134264 (ILLUMINATE) was terminated for increased mortality/cardiac events. The death incidence (1.23% torcetrapib+atorvastatin vs 0.78% atorvastatin; HR 1.58) is the trial's reported all-cause-mortality result; the +5.4 mmHg BP rise and the potassium/sodium/bicarbonate/aldosterone shifts are continuous off-target findings captured as safety_signals because they are not per-arm incidences.
